[[File:Nicole Spillane Oberwolfach 2014.jpg|thumb|Spillane at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2014]]
'''Nicole Spillane''' (born 2 January 1988) is a French and Irish applied mathematician. She is a researcher with the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) in France, where she works in the center for applied mathematics of the [[École Polytechnique]]. Her research concerns [[parallel algorithm]]s for solving large [[system of linear equations|systems of linear equations]].{{r|cv}}

== Career ==
Spillane studied for an engineering diploma at the [[École des ponts ParisTech]] from 2006 to 2010. Over the same period she visited [[Stanford University]] and the [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre]], and earned a master's degree in mathematics from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]]. She completed her doctorate in applied mathematics at Pierre and Marie Curie University in 2014.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Méthodes de décomposition de domaine robustes pour les problèmes symétriques définis positifs'', was jointly supervised by Frédéric Nataf and Patrice Hauret.{{r|mgp}} After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Chile]], she joined CNRS and the École Polytechnique in 2015.{{r|cv}}

In 2017 the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] gave Spillane their [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]].{{r|fox|cnrs-fox}}
